agency: ICER (independent, non-governmental); no national HTA body for reimbursement
threshold_local: USD 100,000-150,000 per QALY or evLYG (ICER value assessment framework)
threshold_note: No binding threshold; Medicare negotiation under the Inflation Reduction Act may not use QALY-based thresholds
source: ICER Value Assessment Framework 2023; Murphy et al 2026 (HEPL)

threshold_local: JPY 5 / 7.5 / 10 million per QALY (ordinary products); JPY 7.5 / 11.25 / 15 million per QALY (orphan, paediatric and anticancer products)
threshold_note: Cost-effectiveness evaluation adjusts the price of selected listed products; it does not determine reimbursement. NHI listing follows approval within 60 days (at most 90)
source: MHLW notification on cost-effectiveness evaluation (2026 edition); Murphy et al 2026 (HEPL)

threshold_local: No cost-per-QALY threshold; added-benefit assessment (AMNOG) followed by price negotiation with GKV-SV; efficiency-frontier method available
threshold_note: Reimbursable from launch; manufacturer-set price for the first six months since 2023 (GKV-FinStG)
source: Murphy et al 2026 (HEPL); Gandjour 2023 (k estimate EUR 88,107 per LYG)

threshold_local: No cost-per-QALY threshold; efficiency opinion informs price negotiation
threshold_note: Early-access programme funds selected products before listing

threshold_local: GBP 20,000-30,000 per QALY to March 2026; GBP 25,000-35,000 from March 2026 (statutory instrument; the 25% figure in the UK-US deal reflects the threshold change plus a new EQ-5D value set); highly specialised technologies GBP 100,000 (weighted 1-3)
threshold_note: Severity modifier x1.2 / x1.7; empirical health opportunity cost GBP 12,936 per QALY at 2008 expenditure (Claxton et al 2015)
source: DHSC/DBT press release, December 2025 (values); UK government consultation response, March 2026 (power of direction); CRA/ABPI 2026; Claxton et al 2015

threshold_local: No cost-per-QALY threshold in AIFA dossier guidelines
threshold_note: Innovativeness assessment determines fund access and early availability

agency: CDA-AMC (formerly CADTH); pCPA price negotiation; provincial listing
threshold_local: CAD 50,000 per QALY used as a reference in reimbursement recommendations
threshold_note: Guidelines refer to a supply-side threshold; price reductions to reach CAD 50,000 per QALY are commonly recommended
source: Murphy et al 2026 (HEPL); Rawson 2026 (Canadian Health Policy)

threshold_local: No explicit threshold; implied acceptance range around AUD 45,000-75,000 per QALY (Harris et al 2008); empirical health opportunity cost AUD 28,033 per QALY (Edney et al 2018)
threshold_note: PBS listing follows PBAC recommendation, price negotiation and, above AUD 20 million per year, Cabinet approval; usually about five months after recommendation
source: Harris et al 2008; Edney et al 2018; Murphy et al 2026 (HEPL); PBS 2026

agency: HIRA (Drug Reimbursement Evaluation Committee) / NHIS price negotiation
threshold_local: Approximately one times GDP per capita per QALY in practice (Bae et al 2016), applied flexibly for oncology and rare diseases
threshold_note: Statutory timelines: HIRA evaluation 150 days, NHIS negotiation 60 days; risk-sharing and exemption pathways exist
source: Bae et al 2016; Zhang and Garau 2020 (OHE)

agency: FOPH (BAG) with the Federal Drug Commission (EAK)
threshold_local: No formal threshold; Federal Supreme Court (BGE 136 V 395, 2010) cited about CHF 100,000 per life-year gained as an order of magnitude
threshold_note: Price set by therapeutic cross-comparison and external reference pricing; case-by-case reimbursement under Art. 71a-d KVV not counted as listing
